genZNote: C. neoformans's relative, except this one goes after immunocompetent hosts too — the exception that makes the rule worth stating.

morphology.size: ~4-6 µm (cell), capsule can extend total diameter to 25 µm or more
morphology.notes: Surrounded by a thick polysaccharide capsule visible on India ink preparation as a clear halo

habitat.naturalHabitat: Associated with certain eucalyptus and other tree species; soil enriched with decaying wood
habitat.hostAssociation: Environmental saprophyte; causes disease in both immunocompetent and immunocompromised hosts (unlike C. neoformans, which favors immunocompromised hosts)
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Historically tropical/subtropical, notably eucalyptus-associated; also established in temperate regions such as the Pacific Northwest of North America

microscopy.appearance: Encapsulated budding yeast with a clear halo around the cell

culture.media: Sabouraud dextrose agar; canavanine-glycine-bromothymol blue (CGB) agar to differentiate from C. neoformans
culture.pigmentation: Turns CGB agar medium blue (positive), unlike C. neoformans

identificationClues: Encapsulated yeast visualized with India ink
Turns CGB agar blue — distinguishes from C. neoformans (does not change color)
Can cause pulmonary and CNS disease in apparently healthy, immunocompetent hosts
Latex agglutination/lateral flow assay detects cryptococcal capsular antigen

diseases: Cryptococcomas (mass lesions in lung or brain)
virulenceFactors: Melanin production (protects against oxidative host defenses)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Inhalation of desiccated yeast cells or basidiospores from environmental sources (notably eucalyptus trees and decaying wood)
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Unlike C. neoformans, notable for causing serious disease in immunocompetent individuals; recognized outbreaks in the Pacific Northwest region of North America since the late 1990s
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: CGB agar and molecular methods distinguish it from the closely related but epidemiologically distinct C. neoformans

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Urease positive; CGB agar turns blue
examFacts.importantDisease: Cryptococcal meningitis/pulmonary cryptococcosis in immunocompetent hosts
examFacts.importantTest: India ink preparation; CGB agar; cryptococcal antigen test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Causes disease in immunocompetent hosts, unlike C. neoformans, which predominantly affects the immunocompromised
